To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the D-JC structure of XLA B cells was fully functional for subsequent rearrangement of the VH gene, and that failure in the X-linked agammoglobulinemia (XIA) is susceptible to correction by cell fusion.

the B cells from the X-linked agammglobulinemia (XAG) patients, who lack B cell development due to failure of immunoglobulins (Igs) rearrangement, can be rescued from the disease state through cell fusion with myeloma cells.

the B cells from XLA patients have a functional D-J-C(mu/ delta) heavy chain, that the VH gene can be expressed by this heavy chain, and that the XLA B cell is susceptible to correction of its immunoglobulin deficiency by cell fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular basis of X-linked agammglobulinemia.
the molecular and cellular basis of the human X-linked agammalglobulinemia, XLA, which is the most common inherited immunodeficiency disorder in humans.
the molecular mechanisms of B cell development and immunoglobulin gene regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular defect in XLA is a defect in the VH gene rearrangement mechanism.
the XLA B cell is not a terminally differentiated lymphocyte but rather a B cell that is blocked in its differentiation at a very early step.
the molecular defect in the X-linked agammglobulinemia (XIA) is a failure to rearrange the VH gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular defect in X-linked agammeglobulinemia is the failure of the B lymphoid cell to rearrange a VH gene to the D-JH gene.
the defect of the B lymphocytes from patients with the minor form is not in the rearrangement of the D-J-C(mu) gene, but is in the rearrangement or function of the VH gene.
the defect in XLA is correctable by fusion with myeloma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the D-J-C structure is fully functional and can support the rearrangement of a V(D)J gene element.
it is possible to correct the molecular defect in a B lymphocyte from a patient with X-linked agammoglobulinemia (XIA) by cell fusion.
the D-J-C(mu) structure is fully capable of rearranging to a V(D)J gene element.
